definition_for_your_team: The person inside the account who wants this to happen and will spend political capital on it. Not the same as the main contact.
The person who can sign or kill the budget. If they have not been in a conversation, the field stays empty.
Confirmed only when the buyer states a number or an approved line. 'We have budget for tools like this' is discussed, not confirmed.
The buyer's stated decision or go-live date, in their words, with the source line.
example_value: Pilot by November; contract before fiscal year end

definition_for_your_team: What the buyer said they will judge on. Verbatim where possible.
example_value: SOC 2 report; HubSpot native; under 2 weeks to live

definition_for_your_team: Who signs, in what order, and what the procurement or security steps are.
example_value: Security review then CFO sign-off then legal

definition_for_your_team: The strongest reason they gave for not buying, and whether it was answered.
example_value: Worried about rep adoption; addressed with the no-change-to-workflow point

definition_for_your_team: Any named alternative, including 'do nothing' and 'hire someone'.
The specific action both sides agreed to, with the date. Not 'follow up'.
example_value: Send SOC 2 to Maria by Thursday; 20-min CFO call next week

definition_for_your_team: Every person named in any conversation, with an inferred role: champion, economic buyer, technical evaluator, blocker, end user.
Your segments in your language, not a NAICS code.
How closely this account matches the profile you defined.
What they are trying to do, in their words.
example_value: Stop losing renewals to late follow-ups

definition_for_your_team: Missing decision-maker; budget uncertainty; competitive threat; timeline drift; champion disengagement. Each with severity and source line.
Inbound, outbound, referral, partner. Keep it honest; it feeds the win/loss analysis.
The last two-way interaction, any channel. Not the last email you sent.
